title: tbc
body:
There tends to be a lot of tension between when people are looking for truthfulness or support. In a medium where ego is attached such as art, appearance, almost any subjective category we are often forced to consider whether expressing our opinions fully is acceptable by the recipient. Not having a grasp on the other's desire when reaching out for input creates a tension between the desire and the result. If someone is elated to discuss their advanced skill in a field while an outside user can see they fundamentally lack skill we may still feel pressure to overinflate their progress to match their excitement as to prevent tension. I think this creates a lot of paranoia in myself where I am wondering if when sharing traits, skills, lessons, and otherwise with peers I will be provided with an insincere perspective which will bolster my perspective rather than expand my view of the mentioned. It becomes a game of seeking truth from those you trust, a seemingly losing battle at that. To both provide and receive perspectives with peers has so much emotional weight tied to it. I am fearful of entering a stasis in my efforts due to this effect. When requesting feedback from those around me I tend to favor honesty. Many people I know do not, and attach so much of their ego to the request that to provide true input would be seen as treasonous to the relationship. The problem is when the latter person exists the natural reaction  is to avoid friction and present the most agreeable perspective to the requestor. 

Even when presenting a more true opinion we often sheath our perspective in padding trying to dissociate ourselves from the opinion. "I like it, but it's not for me". There is so much of a barrier between the things we truly feel and actually express in these moments that I no longer find myself seeking it from others. Unless a quantifiable piece of information can tell me one way or another.
